title: Who runs the A/C at the swap
ask: At the swap, should the ECU (EMU PRO) switch the A/C clutch and read the pressure sensor, with the DCU only sending the A/C request over CAN?
why: Your D-324 puts the A/C clutch on a DCU comfort output and the pressure sensor on a DCU input. The DCU board now drawn (electrical D-452) uses every Teensy pin and has no analog input left. The EMU PRO has the inputs, and it needs to know about the A/C anyway, for idle-up and to cut the compressor at full throttle.
options:
(a) The ECU owns the clutch and the pressure sensor; the DCU's A/C key becomes a CAN request. No DCU change.
(b) Keep D-324: redesign the DCU board now with one more low-side output and an analog input, by dropping something else or adding a second expander and an ADC chip.
recommend: (a), unless you want the A/C to work with the ECU unplugged
stops: Engine D-324, HO13, LW32/LW33 and the DCU carrier layout (electrical H-002)

title: A seventh plug at the dash post for the engine's optional wires
ask: Should the swapped engine's leg get one more small plug at the dash post, so the airflow meter, the cam phaser and the neutral switch each keep a place?
why: You chose six 12-way plugs as room for every option (D-443). That count assumed the two plugs at the post today were empty at the swap; they are not. Five of their cavities are wired to the cluster, the power unit or a fused 12 V supply and can never carry an engine wire (tach, water-temperature gauge, the park/neutral input, the sensor supply, the cluster's spare input), and the corrected plan adds three wires (the brake fluid switch, a road-speed shield drain, the alternator command). With every option the leg needs 71 places and six plugs have 67 usable. Today the airflow meter (MAF), the cam phaser pair (VVT) and the neutral switch pair have none. The dash post's panel is being laid out now (electrical E13) with room for four extra receptacles; a seventh plug needs a fifth.
options:
(a) Add a seventh plug, a 6-way DT pair (about $10-20, confirm), and leave room for a fifth receptacle on the dash post panel now. Every option keeps a place, with one spare. Forecloses nothing; costs a little panel room.
(b) Stay at six plugs. The airflow meter, cam phaser and neutral switch get a place only if another option is dropped first - the O2 sensors or purge if the emissions check allows (K2), or two A/C sensor wires if the ECU runs the A/C (block 02.15). Costs nothing; forecloses an LC9 with its cam phaser together with the full emissions set.
recommend: (a), unless the dash post panel has no room for a fifth receptacle when it is measured
stops: K6's last five conductors (LW24 MAF, LW34 VVT, LW38 neutral switch), D-443's plug count, and the panel room electrical E13 leaves at the post

title: A low-coolant warning after the swap
ask: Should the swapped engine get a coolant level switch in its expansion tank that lights a warning on the cluster screen?
why: The 12A has a coolant level sensor in the radiator (00-CAR PT292, you confirmed it at 00-verify B26) that lights a warning lamp. It leaves with the 12A's radiator, and nothing in the swap plan replaces it. Without one, the engine computer's coolant temperature is the only guard, and a leak shows only once the engine is already running hot - on aluminum heads. A place for the switch already exists: the reserved cavity L1-S2 11 at the dash post runs to the cluster's spare input (IC17), so no new cavity is needed.
options:
(a) Fit a coolant level switch in the swap's expansion tank (about $20-40, confirm), wired through L1-S2 11 to the cluster's spare input, with a warning on the screen. Uses the spare input; if the wideband gauge later needs that input as its fallback (electrical B2), the switch moves to an engine-computer input and the warning comes over CAN.
(b) No level switch: the engine computer's over-temperature warning and protection are the only guard. Costs nothing; a slow leak is seen only as heat.
recommend: (a), unless you would rather rely on the temperature warning alone
stops: The swap's use of L1-S2 11 (HO09), the coolant level rows in ls_devices / ls_wires, and the swap's parts list (DS10)
